prompt:
Generate a high-fidelity desktop product UI design proposal for Hirsel, a personal AI agent workspace. Produce a clean landscape comparison image, approximately 1800 by 1000, showing TWO equally large usable app screenshots side by side, left = global Hirsel conversation, right = a focused Thread. Small neutral labels OUTSIDE the app screenshots say "GLOBAL" and "IN A THREAD"; these labels are for the comparison only. This is an application design comp, not a poster, not a device photograph.
Use the provided current-app screenshot ONLY for the established very pale mint background, dark slate text, Inter-like typography, quiet borders, small geometric brand mark, and restrained professional character. Do NOT copy its crowded text navigation, redundant headings, fixture names, timestamp suffixes, repeated artifact cards, or its precise layout. Keep a light theme in both screenshots.
User requirements: substantial space saving through compact, well-spaced line-icon BUTTONS for utilities: create thread plus, artifacts document/grid, activity pulse, settings gear, overflow ellipsis. Icons have clear button hit areas, one active indicator; no text label next to every utility icon. Thread names and conversation prose remain readable text. Minimal chrome, generous conversation space, no huge title banners. The global orchestrator has NO page title and NO "Orchestrator" heading. Distinguish a focused Thread through STRUCTURE and a clear navigation/context cue, not just changing the title and not color alone. A Thread may have a small name in its context cue. Composer stays at the bottom in both contexts. Show a paperclip button and an upward-arrow send button in the composer.
Sample global conversation: owner "What should I pick up next?" and Hirsel "The architecture note is ready to review." A single compact referenced artifact row named "Architecture note" with a document icon and an open arrow. Sample focused Thread: owner "Make the recommendation simpler." Hirsel "I narrowed it to one approach and updated the note." One compact artifact reference. No charts, marketing statistics, decorative blobs, gradients, huge rounded cards, extra dashboards, or invented notifications.
OPTION A — ICON RAIL AND FOCUS FRAME. Give each screenshot a permanent very narrow 52px vertical global icon rail at left: geometric Hirsel home button at top, threads branching-lines icon, artifact grid icon, activity pulse, settings at bottom. Thread picker is a drawer opened from the rail, CLOSED in these screenshots. Global conversation is an open flat canvas starting immediately after the rail, with no content header. In the focused screenshot show a distinct inset work surface with a fine visible frame and a narrow compact context strip: back arrow, branching thread glyph, small "Architecture plan", overflow icon. A small connected notch/line linking rail's selected Threads icon to the focus frame reinforces entering a specific work context. Conversation/artifact switch is just a small pair of outlined icon buttons in the context strip, selected conversation indicated by shape/fill, with a subtle tiny artifact count. Keep global home visibly selected on left, Threads icon visibly selected on right. This is the most compact recommended direction: no permanent text sidebar, no repeated "Message to..." text.
approved_adjustments: Omit duplicate global top utility buttons; each utility lives once in the icon rail.
GLOBAL and IN A THREAD label the comparison only; ship one application view according to the focused Thread.
